definition: Audible means able to be heard.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word audible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know audible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Bats hunt by cries pitched too high to be audible to us; the night forest is full of shouting we cannot hear.
A faint sound sits at the very edge of hearing — you can't swear it's there; audible crosses the line: it can actually be heard.
Blaring is far past audible — not merely hearable but flooding the whole street, impossible not to hear.

Perceptible means noticeable by any sense at all — a perceptible chill on the skin, a perceptible flicker at the corner of the eye. Audible makes the narrower claim: this thing can be heard, specifically, by an ear. Everything audible is perceptible, but only through one particular door.

Detectable says something can be picked up by whatever is doing the detecting — an instrument, a dog's nose, a lab test — with no ear required. Audible stakes its whole claim on human hearing: a sound an ear can catch. A gas leak may be detectable by sensors while staying perfectly silent.
